fullResponse:
Final report for frozen scope review-01, now including the new evidence. All file references are to the frozen tree at `_build/terrain-presentation-20261017/review-01/tree/`, which matches the working tree for the reviewed directories. Inspection was read-only: file reads, greps, one tree diff and a JSON summary of the observation files. No build, test, edit, memory update or delegation. The stop notifier was not invoked.

## Verdict on frozen01

The scope correctly fixes the two reproduced defects and I recommend no change to its production lines other than the sky brightness item below. Root visibility no longer depends on transport completion at `client/src/scene.js:144`. The adapter keeps the physical binding during loading at `client/src/world-scene.js:255`, and the local command gate sits after the XR mask and clearance checks at `client/src/controlled-navigation.js:137`. The new evidence agrees: the corrected Erlang fixture passed all three real-owner cases, and the live browser run with the current bundle showed no fully hidden frame across three interest crossings.

**Verified sound.** Movement remains gated locally and at `client/src/simulation.js:115`. Stale manifests release only their own credit and never touch retained rows at `simulation.js:199-202`. Catalogue reads cross two signed ACLs that admit the conjunction form, `priv/ontologies/quod_lobby.pl:6,17` and `priv/ontologies/quod_material_eidolons.pl:5,13`. World creation, palette freeze and sky instance are one transaction at `priv/ontologies/lobby_worlds.pl:79-105`, and the sky member carries every attribute `priv/ontologies/lobby_instance.pl:96-102` requires. The dome recentre runs between the view matrix update and active-mesh evaluation in Babylon 9.18.1. The camera keeps its default far plane. Docs match code.

**The freeze and jump is not caused by this scope.** The server holds pose delivery until the whole manifest completes: `src/quod_physics.erl:923-933` sends a pose only when `terrain_complete` is true or nothing is wanted, and both frames and resources share one credit at lines 891 to 916. Before this fix the same stall was masked because the terrain was hidden. The scope makes a pre-existing protocol property visible. Shipping frozen01 alone changes the user experience from blank terrain plus frozen pose to visible terrain plus frozen pose and a jump. Whether that intermediate state is acceptable is Yan's call, and the stop request on the campaign is consistent with one scope per commit.

## Confirmed defect

**World sky brightness doubles the panorama.** `lobby_worlds.pl:100` asserts brightness 1000 while the lobby sky uses 120 at `quod_lobby.pl:54`. In sky mode `client/src/render-resources.js:325,343` sets both the emissive colour to albedo times emission and the emissive texture to the panorama, and Babylon adds emissive after the unlit guard closes. The dome renders tint times texture times two, clipping a tonemapped panorama toward white. The value was chosen so the fog colour at `world-scene.js:116` equals the tint, so one number now serves two meanings. Fog should take the tint alone, or brightness should keep the lobby scale. Confirmed by code reading. No run has shown a new sky live.

## Risks, including those raised by the new evidence

- **The planned fairness refactor will break the client as frozen.** Every in-flight terrain handler checks object identity at `simulation.js:169`, and each accepted frame replaces that object through `advance` at `simulation.js:266` and `client/src/signed-view.js:88-89`. Today this is safe only because the single credit guarantees no frame arrives while a chunk, manifest or completion is outstanding. Once frames interleave, a frame during the digest await at `simulation.js:231` drops the chunk without install or ack, and a frame during the render awaits at lines 214, 241 and 246 drops the ack. The result is a stalled window or an `incomplete manifest` failure. The server change needs a matching client change that identifies liveness by epoch and view rather than object identity. Flag this before the refactor starts.
- **Refactor invariants to preserve.** Acknowledgements must still release only their own token, as `quod_physics.erl:178-191` enforces, and the frame ack clause at lines 174-176 must stay distinct from resource acks. Fairness must not let a stale window's chunks or completion mark the newer interest ready.
- **Loading time under streaming.** The first window in the headless runs took far longer than the hidden-root baseline, with movement blocked throughout. Visible chunks make each software-rendered frame heavier while the per-chunk stop-and-wait credit serialises delivery with rendering. The parent's timing trace should separate frame cost from round trips, and a real GPU measurement is needed before any claim about acceptable wait.

| Run | First window, manifest to complete |
|---|---|
| baseline-01, root hidden | 1.4 s |
| streaming-preview-03 | 13.1 s |
| streaming-preview-04 | 14.8 s |

- **Coasting under the last drive lease.** When loading begins, the client stops renewing drive at `controlled-navigation.js:137` but sends no stop, so the body keeps moving until the lease expires, hidden behind the frozen pose and revealed by the jump. Fairness alone will reveal the coast instead of the jump. Consider an explicit stop on entering the loading state.
- **Renewal projections still blank the terrain.** The view lifetime is five minutes at `client/src/signed-client.js:8`. Each renewal nulls the terrain at `simulation.js:163` and hides the root at `scene.js:117` until a fresh manifest arrives. Retained rows already carry body and revision, and `scene.js:119-120` filters on them, so an equal body revision could keep showing verified chunks without an exception path.
- **Dome depth order is implicit.** The dome writes no depth and Babylon orders opaque meshes by material unique id. A later sky surface change recreates the material at `scene.js:249-251`, after which the forty-metre dome overdraws terrain beyond its radius, which exists at coarse spacing.
- **Local suppression covers drive only.** Jump, snap and teleport at `controlled-navigation.js:29-34,176-178,189-196` still issue refused commands while loading, and snap and teleport call `reset()` first, clearing held input.
- **Live genesis dependencies.** `world_palette/1` needs `material_eidolons/2` in the live quod:lobby, which no source file provides. The existing `material_surface/2` already depends on it, so parity is likely. Older personal lobbies may lack `environment_eidolons/2`, in which case `lobby_instance.pl:124-126` fails and `priv/ontologies/space_view.pl:35-36` shows a "No matching eidolon" label instead of a sky.

**Evidence limits.** No run has exercised a new world with textures and a sky. Both passing preview runs entered the pre-existing world. Physics-credit focused runs one and two failed with `install_missing` and an unexpected `terrain_complete` reply before run three passed, and I did not analyse those failures. Preview runs one and two timed out before readiness and are not evidence. I did not recompute the source manifest hashes. The frozen tree carries a large uncommitted predecessor delta against HEAD across twenty files, outside this review. This review is consultative, not approval.
